state-foia-c09001239.ask: Transcribe the typed text of this letter: the date, the classification marking under it, the salutation, the body, and the address block. Leave out the DECLASSIFIED stamps, the page number and the marking at the foot of the page.
state-foia-c09001239.text: June 30, 1958 SECRET My dear Friend: I have your letter of June 16 in reply to mine of May 22. I have already regretfully replied by cable to that part of it which suggested that I might come to Bonn and talk with you following my meeting with General de Gaulle. Because of an engagement to go to Canada with President Eisenhower, I can only spend 24 hours in Europe, arriving in Paris late Friday afternoon and leaving Saturday night immediately following a dinner which I am giving for the Foreign Minister. I am the more sorry because I really feel that there is a need for us to have a good talk together to keep our thinking in harmony. Written communications are no adequate substitute. However, I will try to put down a few thoughts, particularly about the subject of disarmament which preoccupies us all so much these days. The inherent difficulty of the problem is immensely increased by the fact that we are dealing with those who are utterly undependable and who deliberately make agreements which they can later break to our undoing. There is a very long list of nations and of people who have come to an untimely end by relying upon Soviet promises. The Baltic States were among the earlier, and Nagy among the more recent, victims of relying upon Communist promises. If, therefore, we heed the lesson which has been taught so many times, we must be very careful. This in turn creates problems because of the inordinate complexity of the elements of military power. That makes it almost impossible to arrive at disarmament agreements which have equal military implications for both sides, and which are 100% dependable as regards supervision and enforcement. His Excellency Dr. Konrad Adenauer, Chancellor of the Federal Republic of Germany, Bonn.
state-foia-c09001239.notes: Transcribed from a 300 dpi render. 'har-mony' is joined across the line break.

usgs-wsp-1050.notes: The table is printed sideways. Its header is on p247; these rows are on p248, which repeats no header, so each value has to be placed by the column rules of p247. In four rows one value spans sodium and potassium; it's keyed under sodium (the prompt asks for that) and potassium accepts either the value or empty.
